fallbackFor: Grok 4.6 timed out on the first planning phase; the owner authorized Opus 5 OAuth whenever Grok has an issue
summary: Opus 5 OAuth fallback adversarial planning audit (Grok 4.6 timed out; this is NOT Grok evidence and does not satisfy any mandatory-Grok workflow rule). Verdict: REVISE. The packet is directionally strong and, importantly, contains no P0: it does not authorize implementation, select a provider, invent numeric thresholds, merge appointment authority into website release, or claim a mechanical pass from model review. Result vocabulary (PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT_RUN), evidence binding, baseline-before-threshold discipline, and Page IR inheritance-not-duplication are genuinely well constructed. However, the three target files do not yet deliver the traceability they promise. (1) manifest.json's schema omits the exact fields the strategy's own evaluation contract declares mandatory before a ticket is `ready` (evaluation owner, fixture/environment, evidence path and retention class, policy/toolchain binding, expiry, human-vs-deterministic oracle type), so PROG-EVAL-TEST-001 cannot validate what it claims to validate. (2) Four strategy families — CANVAS, CLIENT, QUAL, and the standalone APPT/OPS scope — have no manifest evaluation ID, tier, ticket, or blocking flag, leaving Canvas designer workflow, client review/collaboration, and agency-grade release quality (accessibility, SEO, performance, security headers, visual) without an owner even though the supplied compatibility matrix makes them Release 1 exit blockers. (3) traceability.md assigns OBX-P160 (EOS-005 desktop/browser isolation), OBX-P185 (EOS-008 ExperienceModule boundary) and OBX-P170 (EOS-007) to tickets that no manifest evaluation carries, so 3 of 19 gaps are traceable only on paper. (4) PROG-EVAL-SEC-001 is a meta-oracle ("every applicable threat domain has an owner, fixture, negative test") covering six EOS gaps under one ticket — existence, not a pass/fail condition. (5) PROG-EVAL-UX-001 is blocking:true with no pass criteria, contradicting the packet's own "a command name is not an evaluation" rule. (6) "T1 is merge-blocking" is stated as fact while supplied reviewer-roles evidence records that the live ruleset requires zero approving reviews and CODEOWNERS is deferred. Secondary contradictions: T4/T5 tiers have zero bound evaluations while T3 absorbs drills; SC-001 puts SBOM/vulnerability response in the credential-free T1 tier the strategy assigns to T2/T3; retention rules (90-day raw model artifacts vs product-lifetime repository history) have no named store and no deletion mechanism; flake handling has no detection, retry, or quarantine-registry mechanism; the mandatory-Grok review rule has no fallback clause, which this very audit exercises. Fixes are bounded and documentation-level; no implementation, schema change, provider, invitation, or appointment authorization is granted or implied.

findings.issue: The strategy's evaluation contract requires every requirement to map to "a stable evaluation ID, a ticket, an evaluation owner, a fixture or environment, a method, a blocking rule, and an evidence-retention class before its ticket can become `ready`", and results to bind commit, source authority, candidate/release identity, fixture/manifest version, toolchain, environment, and policy version. The manifest schema (schemaVersion 1) carries only id, title, tier, method, blocking, status, requirements, ownerTicket, oracle. There is no field for evaluation owner (human/role), fixture or corpus identity, evidence path, retention class, toolchain/policy binding, expiry, or oracle type (deterministic vs named-human).
findings.risk: PROG-EVAL-TEST-001's oracle ("a deliberate missing link, stale receipt, or unauthorized human-review result fails validation") cannot be implemented against this schema: stale receipts and unauthorized human results are not representable. The 'ready' precondition and 'stale evidence is not inherited' rule become unverifiable prose, and the program's central traceability claim degrades to a hand-maintained table.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Extend schemaVersion to add required fields per evaluation: evaluationOwnerRole, fixtureOrEnvironment, evidencePath, evidenceRetentionClass (keyed to the strategy's retention table), oracleType (deterministic|human|hybrid), bindsTo (commit, sourceAuthority, candidateOrRelease, fixtureVersion, toolchain, environment, policyVersion), and expiry. Mark them required-before-`ready` rather than required-now, so planned entries stay valid.

findings.issue: The strategy defines PROG-EVAL-CANVAS (selection, hierarchy, responsive view, history, diff, restore, asset and typed mutation, plus named-designer review) and PROG-EVAL-CLIENT (candidate-locked invitations, guest least privilege, revocation, stale approval invalidation, comment provenance, actor/event integrity, conflict handling, cursor privacy, screen-share boundaries, transcript consent). Neither family has any manifest evaluation ID, tier, blocking flag, or owner ticket. MOTION-001 covers motion only; UX-001 covers usability study only; SEC-001 lists EOS-007 but its oracle is generic.
findings.risk: Two of the highest-risk product surfaces — the single-writer Canvas mutation path and client-facing review with media/consent — have no blocking program evaluation, no tier assignment, and no ticket. Canvas and client-review work could reach `ready` with no oracle, and the compatibility matrix's client-review revocation/no-mutation evidence requirement has no manifest owner.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Add PROG-EVAL-CANVAS-001 (T2, blocking, requirements EOS-004/EOS-014 as applicable) and PROG-EVAL-CLIENT-001 (T2, blocking, requirements EOS-007) with concrete oracles and distinct owner tickets, and reference them from traceability.md.

findings.issue: PROG-EVAL-QUAL (accessibility, SEO, structured data, metadata, link/asset integrity, performance budgets, responsive layout, forms/runtime adapters, privacy/consent, security headers, copy completeness, visual quality, deployment conformance, runbooks) has no manifest evaluation, no T3 ticket, and no owner. The supplied Release 1 compatibility matrix makes accessibility, SEO semantics, and performance baselines explicit Release 1 exit conditions with named blocking behavior ("any blocking accessibility defect blocks qualification/release").
findings.risk: The strategy's own T3 gate ("release authorization") has no evaluation bound to it for the quality dimensions the compatibility matrix says block release. A release candidate could satisfy every manifest entry and still have zero accessibility, SEO, security-header, or visual-quality evidence.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Add PROG-EVAL-QUAL-001 (T3, blocking) with sub-oracles for accessibility, SEO/structured data, security headers, link/asset integrity, and named-human visual quality, an owner ticket, and an explicit split between baseline-establishing runs and threshold-enforcing runs (see F-07).

findings.issue: Traceability assigns EOS-005 (desktop/browser isolation) to OBX-P160, EOS-008 (ExperienceModule boundary) to OBX-P185, and EOS-007 (client review and media) to OBX-P170. No manifest evaluation carries OBX-P160 or OBX-P185 at all; the evaluations named for those rows (PROG-EVAL-SEC-001, PROG-EVAL-SC-001) carry OBX-P130 and OBX-P150. UX-001 owns OBX-P170 but its requirements list only EOS-014, not EOS-007.
findings.risk: Three gaps have an owner ticket that exists nowhere in the evaluation manifest, so the two artifacts disagree about who closes them. Browser/renderer isolation and the ExperienceModule trust boundary — both security-critical — are traceable only through a generic security eval, and the closure rule ("all linked tickets are done") can be satisfied against tickets no evaluation binds.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Either add manifest evaluations owning OBX-P160 (desktop/browser isolation) and OBX-P185 (ExperienceModule boundary) with EOS-005/EOS-008 in their requirements and their own oracles, or change the traceability rows to the tickets the existing evaluations actually own; add EOS-007 to the requirements of whichever evaluation is named its primary owner.

findings.issue: A single blocking T2 evaluation covers EOS-003 through EOS-008 (identity/tenancy, shared mutation, desktop/browser isolation, agent and model routing, client review and media, ExperienceModule boundary) under one ticket, with the oracle "Every applicable threat domain has an owner, fixture, negative test, evidence path, and no unaccepted P0 or P1 finding." That asserts the existence of oracles rather than stating any pass/fail condition, and "applicable" is self-scoped by the party under test. No threat-model document is referenced or hash-pinned.
findings.risk: The packet's largest security claim is unfalsifiable as written: a run could report PASS by demonstrating that fixtures exist. Tenant isolation, SSRF, prompt injection, sandbox escape, worker isolation, and appointment separation each need distinct negative oracles; bundling them behind one meta-assertion permits partial coverage to present as full coverage, and one ticket makes per-domain ownership impossible.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Split PROG-EVAL-SEC-001 into per-domain sub-evaluations (or an enumerated `subOracles[]` array) each with its own negative test, fixture, owner, and pass/fail statement; reference the threat-model document by path and hash; replace "applicable" with an explicit ticket-class-to-domain mapping.

findings.sectionOrLines: PROG-EVAL-UX-001 (and by extension any baseline-first quality gate)
findings.issue: PROG-EVAL-UX-001 is `blocking: true` at T3 with the oracle "the fixed study records completion, time, errors, recovery, discoverability, confidence, and assistance ...; targets are frozen from the baseline before launch." Recording measurements is not a pass condition, and by the packet's own correct baseline-before-threshold rule no targets exist yet. The evaluation therefore has no defined FAIL, directly contradicting the strategy's rule that "a command name is not an evaluation: the oracle must say what constitutes PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, and NOT_RUN."
findings.risk: A blocking release gate that cannot fail either waves work through or is silently treated as satisfied by study completion. The same pattern will recur for accessibility/SEO/performance once those evaluations are added, so the defect is structural rather than isolated to UX.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Split into two entries: a non-blocking baseline-establishing evaluation whose only outcomes are BLOCKED/NOT_RUN/complete-with-data, and a blocking threshold-enforcing evaluation that is `status: blocked` until the owner accepts frozen targets. Apply the same split pattern to every baseline-dependent quality gate.

findings.sectionOrLines: "CI and release policy" — "T1 is merge-blocking and credential-free"; "one non-author technical verification"
findings.issue: The strategy states T1 merge-blocking and non-author verification as current policy, with no present/intended distinction — unlike the "Current executable baseline" table, which carefully separates them. The supplied docs/governance/reviewer-roles.md records the opposite for the actual control point: "The inspected live ruleset had zero required approving reviews", CODEOWNERS enforcement is deferred pending recorded GitHub identities, and "Remote repository enforcement: not changed by this planning packet."
findings.risk: Every downstream traceability and independence guarantee in the packet rests on a merge gate that the supplied evidence says is not enforced. Readers of the strategy alone will believe merges are blocked and independence is required when neither is mechanically true, and no compensating manual control or enforcement ticket is named.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Restate as target state, add one sentence recording the current enforcement status (required approvals: 0; required checks: unverified) as BLOCKED/NOT_RUN, and link a named ticket that configures branch protection and required checks before any T1 evaluation is reported as blocking.

findings.sectionOrLines: "Test and evidence tiers" rows T0/T4/T5 vs manifest `tier` values
findings.issue: The manifest uses only T1, T2, and T3. No evaluation is bound to T4 production verification (exact public-origin bytes, runtime adapters, telemetry/cost, synthetic journeys, rollback readiness; blocks "rollout continuation") or T5 operational drill (backup/restore, provider outage, secret revocation, desktop update/rollback, tenant deletion, incident response; blocks "support-window continuation"). PROG-EVAL-HANDOFF-001 places tabletop/production-like drills including incident, deletion, and offboarding at T3, contradicting the T5 definition.
findings.risk: Two declared gates have no oracle, no owner, and no ticket, so the rollout-continuation and support-window-continuation decisions are undefended. The T3/T5 mismatch means drill evidence may be consumed as release-candidate evidence and never repeated on the scheduled/post-incident cadence T5 requires.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Either add at least one T4 and one T5 evaluation with owner tickets, or mark T4/T5 explicitly as "defined, no evaluation bound in the planning baseline" with the ticket that will populate them; retier the drill portion of HANDOFF-001 to T5 or state why it is a T3 one-off plus a T5 recurrence.

findings.sectionOrLines: PROG-EVAL-SC-001 (tier T1, method "ledger-lockfile-sbom-policy") vs strategy tier table T2/T3 rows
findings.issue: SC-001 sits in the credential-free merge-blocking T1 tier while requiring integrity, license, permissions, vulnerability response, kill switch, and removal plan for every executable dependency, skill, plugin, model, worker image, desktop update, and experience module. The strategy tier table assigns dependency/security scans to T2 and SBOM to T3. No advisory-data source, offline/pinned vulnerability database, or verification method for "kill switch" and "removal plan" is defined.
findings.risk: Either the merge gate silently needs network/credentialed advisory feeds (breaking the credential-free T1 property) or the vulnerability and SBOM portions quietly do not run at T1, making the entry's blocking claim false. Unverifiable sub-items (kill switch, removal plan) invite attestation-by-assertion.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Split SC-001 into a T1 deterministic portion (lockfile pinning, allowlist/denylist, license field presence, ledger completeness — all offline) and a T2/T3 portion (vulnerability response, SBOM), and state the verification method for kill switch and removal plan or mark those as review-only with a named owner.

findings.issue: The table requires merge receipts and normalized audit findings in "repository history or linked durable store for product lifetime" while raw model/audit request and response must be "restricted, 90 days by default". No store is named for the restricted class, no deletion mechanism or owner is given, and no manifest field binds an evaluation's evidence to a retention class. "Client files, recordings, and transcripts" have no maximum period, legal basis, or deletion owner — only "explicit deletion policy" deferred to itself.
findings.risk: If raw model request/response artifacts are stored in repository history (the only durable store the packet names), 90-day deletion is not achievable and the restricted class is unenforceable. Consent-bearing client recordings and transcripts — the highest-sensitivity data in the program — end up with no period, no owner, and no evaluation binding.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Name the restricted store explicitly and state that restricted-class artifacts must not enter repository history; assign a deletion owner and a maximum period (or an explicit BLOCKED marker pending the security/data owner) for client recordings and transcripts; add the retention-class field from F-01 so evaluations bind to a class.

findings.sectionOrLines: "CI and release policy" — flaky tests bullet
findings.issue: "Flaky tests are failures in test reliability. Quarantine needs an owner, expiry, linked incident, compensating gate, and restoration ticket." There is no definition of what identifies a test as flaky (rerun count, flake-rate threshold, observation window), no policy on whether re-running a failed job to green is permitted, no quarantine registry location or schema, and no cap on concurrent quarantines or on quarantine duration.
findings.risk: Without a detection rule and an explicit retry prohibition, the most common failure mode — re-running until green and reporting PASS — remains available and undetectable. Without a registry and cap, quarantine becomes a permanent coverage hole that no check can surface.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Define the flake detection rule (e.g. N reruns on identical bytes producing differing results within a stated window), state whether retries are permitted and how a retried pass is recorded, name the quarantine registry file, and set a maximum quarantine duration and concurrent count that PROG-EVAL-TEST-001 can validate.

findings.issue: The inherited Page IR manifest is referenced by path only, with no version or hash pin, no statement of which inherited evaluation IDs are re-reported in which program tier, and no rule for what happens when an inherited threshold or corpus changes. The strategy says "Existing accepted Page IR thresholds remain in force" without binding to a specific accepted version.
findings.risk: Contradicts the packet's own rule that "stale evidence is not inherited across changed bytes or changed policy": inherited PASS results could silently carry across a changed Page IR manifest, corpus, or threshold. Avoiding duplication is correct, but unpinned inheritance reintroduces the drift duplication was meant to prevent.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Pin the inherited manifest by version and content hash in `inheritedManifests`, state which inherited evaluation IDs are surfaced in T1/T2/T3 program runs, and add a rule that an inherited-manifest hash change invalidates dependent program results until re-run.

findings.path: docs/governance/reviewer-roles.md (as applied by the target packet's review rules)
findings.sectionOrLines: "Separation of duties" and "Review packet" — mandatory Grok 4.6 input and "current Grok receipt"
findings.issue: Grok 4.6 is declared mandatory adversarial review input for named packets and every review packet must include a "current Grok receipt". No freshness window defines "current", and there is no documented fallback or exception path when the mandatory reviewer is unavailable. This audit is exactly that case: it is an owner-authorized Opus 5 OAuth fallback produced after a Grok timeout.
findings.risk: The rule as written cannot be satisfied for this packet, so it is either violated or silently satisfied by substituting a different model's receipt without an owner-recorded exception. Over time this normalizes treating any model receipt as the mandatory one and erodes the (correct) rule that model review is input only.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Add a fallback clause to reviewer-roles: when the mandatory reviewer is unavailable, the receipt is recorded as a named-model fallback with reason, authorizing owner, and expiry, and the packet is marked as carrying a substituted-reviewer exception; define the freshness window for "current".

findings.sectionOrLines: strategy "Result vocabulary" independence sentence; reviewer-roles "Separation of duties" risk-exception paragraph
findings.issue: The strategy requires that "the author cannot be the sole accepting reviewer where the risk matrix requires independence" but does not enumerate which change classes are non-waivable. Reviewer-roles permits one person to hold multiple owner roles and permits a "time-bound risk exception with compensating evidence and an expiry" with no cap on count, no maximum duration, no registry, and no escalation path.
findings.risk: For a small team the exception path is the likely default rather than the exception, so blocking independent verification and named-human design/security acceptance can be routinely waived while the packet still reads as enforcing independence. There is no artifact where an auditor can count outstanding exceptions.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Name the non-waivable classes (at minimum: security/data, release candidate, evaluation oracle/threshold, appointment authority), set a maximum exception duration and a cap on concurrent open exceptions, and name the file where exceptions are registered so a check can enumerate them.

findings.issue: One blocking T3 evaluation under one ticket (OBX-P195) covers both provider selection/conformance and appointment lifecycle independence. The strategy's PROG-EVAL-APPT family separately requires the appointment PRD's own suite plus version-skew, revocation, rollback, re-delivery, duplicate/timeout replay, and runtime-downshift tests, but no manifest evaluation ID exists for it.
findings.risk: Provider authority and appointment authority are required to remain separate decisions; binding them to a single evaluation and a single ticket creates a path where a provider conformance PASS is read as appointment-independence evidence, or where an appointment concern gates a provider decision. The appointment-specific test list also has no owner.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Split into PROG-EVAL-PROVIDER-001 (provider conformance and neutrality) and PROG-EVAL-APPT-001 (appointment independence, version skew, replay, downshift) with distinct tickets, and state explicitly in both oracles that neither result may be used as evidence for the other's authority.

findings.issue: The oracle asserts that "visual motion authoring is absent until the accepted license/runtime decision and non-GSAP oracle exist", naming a specific third-party library and implying a license constraint. No license record, licensing-owner decision, or supply-chain ledger entry is supplied in the packet, and the evaluation's ticket (OBX-P175) is a design ticket rather than the licensing/supply-chain owner's.
findings.risk: A vendor-specific license claim recorded in a manifest without a supporting record is unverifiable evidence in exactly the class the packet says must not be invented, and it routes a licensing decision through a design ticket instead of the licensing/supply-chain owner named in reviewer-roles.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Replace the vendor name with a reference to the licensing decision record (or mark it BLOCKED pending that record), and add a licensing/supply-chain owner ticket link alongside OBX-P175.

findings.sectionOrLines: "Current executable baseline" table and the following paragraph
findings.issue: The preamble says "This table does not claim all of them currently run in CI", yet the Present tier column asserts T0/T1/T1/T1 for several commands and the following paragraph states "`verify:plans` is installed in T1" — both are CI claims. No CI workflow path, commit, or run receipt is bound to those assertions.
findings.risk: A reader cannot tell which Present tier cells are verified and which are intent, so the table's honest disclaimer is undercut by the column it disclaims. Downstream planning may assume gates exist that do not.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Add an evidence column citing the CI workflow path and commit (or `unverified`) for each Present tier cell, and reword the verify:plans sentence to cite the workflow entry that installs it.

findings.issue: The four states are well defined, but there is no state or mechanism for a prior PASS that has been invalidated by changed bytes, changed policy version, or expiry, and no structured way to mark a result advisory rather than blocking (the strategy says advisory evaluations use the same vocabulary but nothing distinguishes them in a receipt).
findings.risk: "Stale evidence is not inherited" has no representation in the result model, so an expired PASS and a current PASS are indistinguishable in stored receipts; an advisory PASS can be read as a blocking PASS.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Either add an EXPIRED/STALE state or require every receipt to carry validUntil plus the policy/fixture versions it was bound to, and add an `advisory: true|false` flag to receipts so advisory results cannot be counted as blocking evidence.

acceptedStrengths: Result vocabulary is genuinely well specified: PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT_RUN with explicit "this is not a pass" language for BLOCKED and NOT_RUN, mirrored exactly in manifest.json `resultStates`.

Baseline-before-threshold discipline is held consistently and correctly: PROG-EVAL-QUAL prose, the non-functional measurement protocol, the UX study, and the supplied compatibility matrix all refuse to invent numeric accessibility, SEO, performance, or usability targets, and require fixture/metric/percentile/sample/tolerance to be frozen before implementation claims success.

Evidence binding is stated at the right granularity — commit, source authority, candidate/release identity, fixture/manifest version, toolchain, environment, and policy version — with an explicit no-inheritance rule across changed bytes or changed policy.

Model authority is correctly bounded: models may challenge a packet and explain failures but cannot manufacture a mechanical pass, approve visual quality, accept risk, or authorize release; the traceability closure rule repeats that a model review alone never closes a gap.
The Page IR manifest is inherited rather than duplicated, satisfying the no-duplication requirement, and existing Page IR thresholds are preserved rather than restated.

Appointment independence is stated as a one-way rule ("Website success never supplies appointment acceptance"), and the compatibility matrix keeps appointment fields, CTA leases, and schema out of Release 1 source and bundle.

Named-human visual review is well specified: fixed 1440x900 / 768x1024 / 390x844 captures plus a live keyboard/screen-reader-capable preview, an enumerated rubric, and a receipt carrying reviewer identity, timestamp, candidate hash, rubric version, notes, and decision.
The non-functional measurement protocol (seven required records) and the prohibition on comparing results collected under different fixed conditions as one trend are strong and directly usable.
Re-delivery is correctly treated as a new release candidate with no inherited evidence, closing the common "small content change" loophole.
The tier table's duration values are explicitly run-time targets with a stated split-or-optimize rule rather than permission to skip coverage.

reviewer-roles.md is honest about external enforcement: it records that the inspected live ruleset had zero required approving reviews and explicitly declines to pretend the target state is already enforced.

The manifest's requirement arrays and traceability's per-gap table cover all 19 EOS gaps at least nominally, and the closure rule (owner-accepted design, tickets done, blocking evals PASS on current evidence, no unaccepted P0/P1, authority manifest updated) is a defensible bar.
missingEvidence: The declared aggregate SHA-256 8b3c76d3806a2ace38dcdd69bd083207802d3ea7caad55b95ea90687a47075de could not be recomputed and the three per-file digests in the packet headers could not be verified; no file-read or shell tooling was available in this review session, so all bytes were treated as supplied-and-untrusted.

docs/eval/page-ir-safe-pipeline/manifest.json was not supplied: its contents, version, hash, evaluation IDs, and accepted thresholds are unverified, so the inheritance claim and "existing accepted Page IR thresholds remain in force" cannot be checked.

No ticket records were supplied for OBX-P100, P110, P120, P130, P140, P150, P160, P170, P175, P180, P185, P190, P195 — existence, named owner, status, Definition-of-Ready fields, and dependencies are all unverified.
The EOS-001 through EOS-019 gap register itself was not supplied, so the gap titles used in traceability.md could not be reconciled with the register's normative text or scope.
No CI workflow file, workflow run receipt, or commit reference was supplied to confirm the "Present tier" column or the claim that verify:plans is installed in T1.
No branch-protection or repository-ruleset export was supplied to confirm the current required checks and required approving reviews beyond the prose assertion in reviewer-roles.md.

No threat-model document was supplied for the domains PROG-EVAL-SEC-001 claims to cover (tenant isolation, authorization, malicious files, SSRF, prompt injection, sandbox, browser/renderer, worker isolation, release integrity, public runtime, appointment separation, retention, deletion, support access).

No named humans exist anywhere in the packet for evaluation owner, security/data owner, design/visual owner, operations/release owner, or independent verifier; roles are defined but unfilled, which is the precondition the independence rules depend on.

No license record, SBOM, dependency ledger, or supply-chain allowlist was supplied, so PROG-EVAL-SC-001's oracle and the motion-runtime license assertion in PROG-EVAL-MOTION-001 have no supporting evidence.

No existing baseline measurements or fixture corpora were supplied for accessibility, SEO, performance, or usability; the first admitted Page IR and template-v1 fixture corpus is named as unresolved in the compatibility matrix.
No evidence store, receipt schema, or retention implementation was supplied, so the retention table's classes cannot be bound to an actual location or deletion mechanism.

No user-research plan was supplied for the two usability studies: participant recruitment, sample size, consent handling, moderator identity, and recording/transcript retention are undefined, and no participant evidence exists or was invented here.
No appointment PRD test suite manifest was supplied, so PROG-EVAL-APPT's "use the appointment PRD's separate suite" could not be verified as pointing at an existing, separately owned suite.

phaseDecision.reason: Seven P1 findings and no P0. The packet is safe in the ways that matter most — it authorizes nothing, invents no thresholds, selects no provider, and keeps model review as input only — but it does not yet deliver the traceability it claims. The manifest schema omits the fields the strategy's own contract makes mandatory before a ticket is `ready` (F-01), so PROG-EVAL-TEST-001 cannot validate stale receipts or unauthorized human results. Canvas, client review/collaboration, and agency-grade release quality have no manifest evaluation, tier, blocking flag, or ticket (F-02, F-03) even though the supplied compatibility matrix makes accessibility, SEO, and performance Release 1 exit blockers. Three of nineteen gaps point at owner tickets no evaluation carries (F-04). The program's largest security evaluation is a meta-assertion rather than an oracle (F-05), one blocking gate has no possible FAIL (F-06), and the merge gate the whole scheme rests on is asserted as fact while supplied evidence says it is unenforced (F-07). These are bounded documentation corrections, not redesign: the tiers, vocabulary, evidence binding, and baseline discipline are sound foundations to correct against. The P2/P3 items may be handled as follow-up once the P1 contradictions are resolved, since several of them (F-08 through F-12) are the same enforceability gap viewed from different sections and will largely close alongside the schema fix.

nextActions: Extend manifest.json schemaVersion with the fields the evaluation contract already requires — evaluationOwnerRole, fixtureOrEnvironment, evidencePath, evidenceRetentionClass, oracleType, bindsTo, expiry — marked required-before-`ready` so existing planned entries stay valid (F-01).

Add the four missing manifest evaluations with tiers, blocking flags, distinct owner tickets, and concrete oracles: PROG-EVAL-CANVAS-001, PROG-EVAL-CLIENT-001, PROG-EVAL-QUAL-001, PROG-EVAL-APPT-001 (F-02, F-03, F-15).

Reconcile traceability.md rows EOS-005, EOS-007, and EOS-008 with the manifest: either create evaluations owning OBX-P160 and OBX-P185 or correct the rows to the tickets the existing evaluations own, and add EOS-007 to its primary evaluation's requirements (F-04).
Decompose PROG-EVAL-SEC-001 into per-domain sub-oracles with individual negative tests, fixtures, owners, and pass/fail statements, and cite the threat-model document by path and hash (F-05).

Split every baseline-dependent quality gate into a non-blocking baseline-establishing evaluation and a blocking threshold-enforcing evaluation held at `status: blocked` until the owner accepts frozen targets — starting with PROG-EVAL-UX-001 (F-06).

Restate the T1 merge-blocking and non-author-verification policy as target state, record the current enforcement status honestly, and link the ticket that will configure branch protection and required checks (F-07).

Resolve the tiering contradictions: bind at least one evaluation each to T4 and T5 or mark them explicitly unpopulated, retier the drill portion of HANDOFF-001, and split SC-001 into an offline T1 portion and a T2/T3 vulnerability/SBOM portion (F-08, F-09).
Name the restricted evidence store, prohibit restricted-class artifacts in repository history, and assign an owner and maximum period for client recordings and transcripts (F-10).
Define the flake detection rule, the retry policy, the quarantine registry location, and caps on quarantine duration and concurrency so PROG-EVAL-TEST-001 can validate them (F-11).
Pin the inherited Page IR manifest by version and hash, and state which inherited evaluation IDs surface in which program tier and what a hash change invalidates (F-12).

Add a documented model-review fallback clause to reviewer-roles.md — reason, authorizing owner, expiry, substituted-reviewer exception marker — and define the freshness window for a "current" receipt; record this Opus 5 OAuth fallback receipt under that clause rather than as a Grok receipt (F-13).
Enumerate the non-waivable independence classes, cap risk-exception duration and concurrency, and name the registry file where open exceptions are counted (F-14).

Supply the missing evidence listed above — the gap register, the inherited Page IR manifest, ticket records, CI workflow and ruleset exports, and the threat model — before any of these evaluations is reported as blocking or any gap is claimed closed.
